title: The optimal partial plank covering conjecture for convex bodies
statement:
Let $K\restriction\mathbb{E}^d$ be a convex body and let $W>0$. A **plank** is a region between two parallel hyperplanes; its width is denoted by $w(P)$. For a finite family of planks $P_1,\ldots,P_n$, suppose that

$$
\sum_{i=1}^n w(P_i)=W.
$$

**Optimal partial plank covering conjecture.** There exists a plank $P$ of width $W$ such that, for every such finite family,

$$
\operatorname{vol}_d\!\left(K\cap\bigcup_{i=1}^n P_i\right)\leq\operatorname{vol}_d(K\cap P).
$$

This conjecture asserts that among all partial coverings of a convex body by planks with prescribed total width, a single plank is always optimal. It generalizes the affirmative result for Euclidean balls and the planar case described in the source, while the statement for arbitrary convex bodies and dimensions remains open.
references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2011–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2211.10886](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.10886), [arXiv:1106.5635](https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.5635).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27483

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2026).
source_name: Egor Bakaev and Alexander Polyanskii, “Optimal partial plank coverings”, arXiv:2607.27483 (2026).
